sources.entry: MacMusicPlayer - A clean, lightweight music player for macOS users. ![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A minimalist menu bar music player for macOS with no Dock icon, which also includes built-in YouTube/SoundCloud downloads.
summary.what_it_does: MacMusicPlayer runs as a menu bar app with no Dock icon and plays local audio files in mp3, m4a, wav, flac, aac, ogg, and aiff formats. It offers Sequential, Single Loop, and Random playback modes, and supports multiple music libraries with quick switching and a Spotlight-style song picker opened with ⌘F. The app remembers the last library and last played track, can launch at login, and has a prevent-sleep toggle. A download window handles YouTube/SoundCloud search and playlist downloads with thumbnails and format selection, which requires yt-dlp and ffmpeg. The interface supports light and dark themes and five languages (English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean).
use_cases: Play local music from the macOS menu bar
Browse and jump to songs by title, artist, or filename
Download YouTube or SoundCloud audio and playlists
Manage several music folders and switch between them
Keep music playing without a Dock window
how_to_run: Or download MacMusicPlayer-arm64.dmg from the Releases page and open it (right-click > Open on first launch)
For DMG users: brew install yt-dlp ffmpeg (needed for downloads)
Configure API URL and API Key in Settings to enable YouTube search (requires a custom search proxy service)
Build from source: make build (Release app into build/)
Build a DMG: make dmg; run tests with swift test
notable: Menu bar only app with no Dock icon
Spotlight-style song picker (⌘F) filtering by title, artist, and filename
Built-in YouTube/SoundCloud download with format selection
Media key control and keyboard shortcuts
Prevent-sleep toggle and launch at login, both on by default
caveats: The DMG is ad-hoc signed, so macOS shows an unidentified developer warning on first launch
YouTube search needs a custom search proxy service; downloads need yt-dlp and ffmpeg installed separately for DMG users
